title: 〜のに (contrast) "although / even though / despite"
meaning: Contrary to expectation; the speaker feels surprise, regret, or dissatisfaction.
simpleExplanation: 〜のに means "even though / although" and carries a feeling: surprise, regret or complaint. 一生懸命勉強したのに、試験に落ちた = I studied hard, yet I failed. The first part is a real fact, and the second part is what actually happened, against your expectation. Nouns and な-adjectives take なのに (日曜日なのに). At the end of a sentence, のに alone shows regret: 言ってくれればよかったのに (you should have told me).
whenUsed: Everyday complaints and disappointments in speech and writing. Because the second clause must be a fact, you cannot follow のに with a request, command, invitation or your own plan; for those use が or けど. Compared with けど, のに is stronger and more emotional.
formation: V-plain + のに: 勉強したのに, 飲んだのに
い-adjective + のに: 寒いのに
な-adjective + なのに: 便利なのに
Noun + なのに: 日曜日なのに
Main clause: a fact (not a request, command or invitation)

diagram.title: のに (purpose) vs のに (contrast) vs ても

rows.label: のに (purpose)
cells: 使う / 便利 / かかる

rows.label: のに (contrast)
cells: 薬を飲んだのに、熱が下がらない

cells: any result, including will and requests
薬を飲んでも、熱は下がらないだろう

examples.ja: 一生懸命勉強したのに、試験に落ちた。
examples.reading: いっしょうけんめい べんきょうしたのに、しけんに おちた。
examples.en: Even though I studied hard, I failed the exam.

examples.ja: 今日は日曜日なのに、会社に行かなければならない。
examples.reading: きょうは にちようびなのに、かいしゃに いかなければ ならない。
examples.en: Even though it's Sunday, I have to go to work.
examples.note: Noun + なのに: a complaint about working on Sunday.

examples.ja: 薬を飲んだのに、熱が下がらない。
examples.reading: くすりを のんだのに、ねつが さがらない。
examples.en: I took medicine, but the fever won't go down.
examples.note: The expected effect did not happen.

examples.ja: もう十二月なのに、あまり寒くない。
examples.reading: もう じゅうにがつなのに、あまり さむくない。
examples.en: Even though it's already December, it isn't very cold.

examples.ja: せっかく料理を作ったのに、誰も食べなかった。
examples.reading: せっかく りょうりを つくったのに、だれも たべなかった。
examples.en: I went to the trouble of cooking, but nobody ate it.
examples.note: せっかく〜のに is a common pairing for wasted effort.

similarGrammar.difference: ても is "even if", hypothetical or general, and allows any second clause. のに is "even though", about a real fact, with emotion.
Same letters, but followed by 使う / 便利 / かかる. The contrast のに is followed by an unexpected result.
Neutral "but". Use them when the second clause is a request, invitation or plan (寒いけど、出かけましょう).

commonMistakes.wrong: 今日は日曜日のに、仕事がある。
commonMistakes.right: 今日は日曜日なのに、仕事がある。
commonMistakes.why: Nouns and な-adjectives need な before のに.

commonMistakes.wrong: 寒いのに、窓を開けてください。
commonMistakes.right: 寒いけど、窓を開けてください。
commonMistakes.why: The clause after のに cannot be a request. Use けど or が.

commonMistakes.wrong: 明日雨が降るのに、試合をします。(hypothetical)
commonMistakes.right: 明日雨が降っても、試合をします。
commonMistakes.why: A future possibility is "even if", which is ても. のに is for something that has really happened or is really so.

usageNotes: のに always carries feeling; for a plain contrast without emotion, use が or けど.
Sentence-final のに: 行けばよかったのに (you should have gone), もっと早く言ってくれればいいのに (I wish you'd told me sooner).
〜のに is common with words of effort or expectation: せっかく, 一生懸命, たくさん, もう.
jlptTips: If the first clause is a completed fact (past tense, もう, せっかく) and the second is a disappointment, choose のに. If the first clause is a possibility (もし, いくら, どんなに), choose ても.
Check the ending of the sentence: 〜てください / 〜ましょう / 〜たい after the blank rules out のに.
